source_review.notes: Reviewed Michael's primary hazard-pointer paper, Fraser's primary EBR thesis, Brown's primary EBR retention/reclamation work, Michael-Scott queue retirement context, Herlihy-Wing linearizability, WG21 P2530R3, the current ISO C++ draft safe-reclamation clause, and current Crossbeam epoch 0.9.20 documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Current API claims are limited to the draft/library sources and no interface is represented as proof of correct caller integration.

evidence: Checked private/live/logically-removed/retired/reclaimable/reused lifecycle states and legal transition path.
Checked hazard slots HP[p,k], protected set H, participant/slot cardinality, epoch announcements, retirement generation, and grace predicate.
Checked retire node/byte rates, oldest protection age, scan time, destruction time, and progress terminology remain empirical or conditional as labeled.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The simplified finite-model epoch predicate is explicitly excluded from being universal production EBR notation.

evidence: Recomputed hazard trace: scan while A is protected reclaims zero; after clear it reclaims exactly one.
Recomputed epoch trace: B@0 is unsafe with participant P active at 0 and safe after P quiesces.
Recomputed examples: 50 MB/s for 30 seconds gives 1,500 MB exposure; 64 participants times two slots is 128; 256 nodes times 192 bytes is 49,152 bytes (48 KiB).
numerical_recomputation.notes: Retention arithmetic is a first-order exposure or nominal batch calculation, not an upper bound without enforced participant/rate/size assumptions.

evidence: Verified load-publish-validate closes the initial-load-to-announcement race before dereference under the hazard publication/scan ordering premise.
Verified a retired node matching an active valid hazard remains ineligible until the final dependent access and clear.
Verified epoch eligibility follows only after all participants capable of holding pre-retirement references quiesce, independent of wall-clock time.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Safety, ABA resistance, host-structure linearizability, operation progress, reclamation progress, and retained-memory bounds are proved or scoped separately.

evidence: Reviewed pause before publication, after publication, after validation, before clear, before unpin, and during scan/grace/shutdown.
Reviewed multiple simultaneous nodes, slot/record exhaustion, nesting, pointer escape, async task migration, blocking callbacks/I/O, cancellation, panic/exception, thread exit, and participant reuse.
Reviewed allocator pools, immediate shutdown reuse, ABA, epoch stall/crash, unbounded registration, large/destructive payloads, batch latency, NUMA, memory cap, and malicious retention.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial coverage spans lifetime safety, lifecycle cleanup, progress, resource bounds, latency, and security behavior.

evidence: The hazard model reclaims only retired nodes absent from the current protected set and retains A while named.
The epoch model reclaims only nodes satisfying its documented finite grace predicate and retains B while the earlier reader is active.
Exact output asserts ordered reclamation A,B, empty retire lists, two eligibility transitions, stalled-reader blocking, and no early free in the model.
invariant_checking.notes: Dictionary participants, trusted calls, indivisible methods, and the simple generation predicate intentionally omit real atomic visibility, cyclic epochs, registration races, and failures.

evidence: Reviewed hazard acquisition, validation, multi-node hand-over, retirement, scan visibility, slot ownership, ABA qualification, and clearing discipline.
Reviewed epoch entry, pointer scope, nesting, retire generations, grace/quiescence, stall retention, task topology, and shutdown.
Reviewed allocation/destruction, progress decomposition, hazard work/cardinality, epoch byte exposure, alternatives, evidence ladder, and all exercise solutions.
proof_review.notes: No structural lock-free claim silently includes allocation, slot registration, scan, grace completion, destructor, bounded retention, or shutdown.

evidence: Hazard and epoch safety arguments are presented as proof structures with explicit publication, lifetime, and lifecycle assumptions.
Complexity and retention calculations identify the bounded parameters needed before they can become bounds.
The finite model, model checking, history checking, sanitizers, fault schedules, stress, and production telemetry are separated by scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No elapsed timeout, scan snapshot, throughput result, sanitizer pass, or absence of a live link is generalized into universal reclamation safety/progress.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python eligibility model passed exact eleven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_reclamation_protocol_model and reproduces named-node retention, post-clear reclamation, pinned-epoch retention, and post-quiescence reclamation.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real threads, atomics, allocators, hazards, cyclic EBR, weak memory, ABA/reuse, arbitrary schedule, race/sanitizer, progress, retention, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives both schemes from the delayed-observer lifetime gap, contrasts per-node and per-interval evidence, and separates safety, ABA, progress, memory bounds, lifecycle, and performance.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed guard/slot ownership, multi-node traversal, registration/exhaustion, nested and async use, allocator/destructor integration, thread exit/cancellation, callbacks, pool/object shutdown, stall policy, metrics, memory caps, alternatives, and rollback gates.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet gives both protocols and their failure boundaries; the executable contrasts identical lifetime outcomes; ten examples cover races and operations; five progressive exercises include calculations and complete designs.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Michael, Fraser, Brown, Scott, Herlihy, Wing, WG21, ISO C++, Crossbeam, Rust, concurrency, memory-safety, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither a concrete hazard/EBR implementation, real atomics or weak-memory ordering, cyclic generation rules, allocator/destructor behavior, ABA freedom, host-structure linearizability, arbitrary schedules, registration/nesting/task/thread lifecycle, bounded reclamation or progress, production retention/latency/throughput/fairness, certification, nor deployment fitness.
